long_biography.plain_text:
Sent from Cuba to study at the University of Miami, Souto helped his family restart its coffee trade by making deliveries while attending classes. After graduating, he worked as a menswear buyer before returning full time to the business a decade later. A supermarket order established broader distribution, while a 1982 trip to New York convinced him to pursue the region's growing Hispanic market.

Rowland Coffee later acquired Café Bustelo and expanded it alongside Café Pilón. Souto, his father and two brothers developed the operation from a modest Miami enterprise into a leading United States espresso producer. They adapted packaging and built sales across Florida and the Northeast. The family sold Rowland's brands and operating business to the J.M. Smucker Company in 2011.
